_sebs.c_: Nobody saw Konrad Sebs arrive. One morning there was simply one more helmet in R-F11, and a quiet rifleman under it.
Konrad Sebs was among the first hundred through the depot gates. The First Wave ribbon is the only clean thing he owns.
The transfer made Konrad Sebs a sniper. He spent the first hour learning where everything belonged, including himself.
Konrad Sebs hummed an old song from home on sentry. From the other side of the wire, very faintly, someone hummed it back.
Konrad Sebs saved half a biscuit for later. Later turned out to be six minutes away.
ma.rley5115: Day 3: Yann "Parson" Rley reached R-F7 with a full packet of cigarettes. Learning everyone's name proved remarkably easy.
no_one_here_to_check: Karel Check was a baker in Saint-Lune until the posters went up. He came to R-F10 with his mother's thimble, and within a day the whole bay knew that he counts everything: steps, shells, stars.
Karel Check, volunteer number 67, received the First Wave ribbon. The quartermaster pronounced the name wrong; he corrected it for the record.
Karel Check opened a parcel addressed in an unfamiliar hand. Inside was a note explaining that the usual letter writer had hurt a wrist. He read that note first.
